To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the share of agricultural or informal workers in adults is a key determinant of income poverty in Turkey, and the share of agricultural workers in adults is the main determinant of non-monetary poverty.

(i) the poor in both monetary and nonmonerary measures have a high share of agricultural workers, (ii) the poor in monetary measure have a low share of workers, and (iii) the poor in non-monterary measure have a high share in the informal sector and low share of workers.
the share of informal workers is the most important factor in explaining poverty in Turkey.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of poor and non-poor groups and the determinants of poverty in the Turkish society.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the identification of the poor by income poverty is not sufficient for policy makers to understand the nature of the poor.
income poverty is not a reliable indicator of material deprivation in Turkey.
there is no single indicator that can be used to identify the poor in Turkey.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the identification of the poor is a complex task.
the share of the poor who are not poor in monetary measure increases in the share of workers, while the share of the non-poor who are poor in non-montery measure increases in the same share.
the share of agricultural workers is the most important variable for the poverty in non-monetary measures in Turkey.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification problem of poor people can be solved by using both monetary (income) and non-monetary (material deprivation) measures.
, while the income poverty measure provides a good approximation of non-monetary poverty at the country level, this is not the case at the regional level.
, while the income poverty rate is low in Turkey, the material deprivation rate is high.
